page: Amazon Web Services m6id.24xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based instance configuration powered by 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors (Ice Lake 8375C). Operating on an x86_64 architecture at 3.5 GHz, the instance delivers 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The platform is paired with 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio (4.0 GB per core). For high-speed local scratch space and caching, it includes 5,700 GB of NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 38 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Hardware acceleration via GPUs is not included.

Benchmark results highlight significant multi-core throughput and strong data caching performance. The server achieves a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 92,888.69 and a PassMark CPU score of 75,234.08, both ranking in the top 25%. Cryptographic execution is particularly capable, with the PassMark CPU encryption benchmark reaching the top 10% (86,161.03), assisted by hardware-level AES, VAES, and SHA-NI flags. Memory bandwidth reaches 4,972.07 GB/sec for cached 16 KB read blocks and 329.31 GB/sec for large 256 MB reads. In real-world service simulations, it recorded 90.26 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 68.96 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Single-core performance reflects moderate architectural baselines, with Geekbench single-core at 1,672.0 and stress-ng single-core at 1,893.08, situating it within the middle 50%. Large-scale CPU inference is constrained, demonstrating weaker throughput for large 70B language models (2.58 tokens/sec text generation) due to the absence of dedicated accelerators. Given the resource density, local NVMe footprint, and balanced compute capabilities, the m6id.24xlarge is well-suited for high-throughput relational databases, in-memory caches, Clang-based software build environments, ETL pipelines, and concurrent web applications.
description: Amazon Web Services m6id.24xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring an Intel Xeon 8375C processor with 96 vCPUs (48 physical cores) operating at 3.5 GHz on the AWS Nitro system. It provides 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory, 5,700 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and 38 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with zero GPUs. Benchmark evaluation demonstrates strong multi-threaded compute, high memory bandwidth, and top-tier cryptographic performance, registering 90.26 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks and 68.96 GB/sec in static web serving. While single-thread execution and large-scale language model inference remain average or weak, its balanced core-to-memory allocation and dense local storage suit enterprise database management, multi-threaded CI/CD builds, and high-concurrency microservice architectures.
